title: Rank Based Routing in Large Server Systems under Extreme Congestion
summary: We study $n$ parallel queues in an extreme heavy-traffic regime: each server works at rate $n$, while jobs arrive to a dispatcher at rate $n^2-(a-b)\sqrt{n}$, with fixed $a>b>0$. Arrivals are routed by a marginal join-the-shortest-queue policy: a small stream of rate $b\sqrt{n}$ joins the current shortest queue, while the remaining stream of rate $n^2-a\sqrt{n}$ is routed uniformly at random. This policy greatly reduces communication cost relative to full JSQ, while improving load balancing and offering a natural mechanism for premium jobs to join shorter queues.
